question:
Consider the pytest test `optuna_qa/pareto_front_get_pareto_front_info_s4_dataflow/files/testcase.py::TestParetoFrontScenarios::test_many_pareto_front_plots` (test class `TestParetoFrontScenarios`, its single test method `test_many_pareto_front_plots`). During this test run the function `optuna.visualization._pareto_front._get_pareto_front_info`, defined in the file `optuna/visualization/_pareto_front.py`, is invoked several times (indirectly, through `optuna.visualization.plot_pareto_front`); some invocations return normally and some raise. An invocation is one call of this function; consider ALL invocations made during the test run (including those that end by raising an exception) and report the union of the def-use pairs observed in them.

Tracked variables (local names of the frame of `_get_pareto_front_info` itself), exactly: `study`, `target_names`, `include_dominated_trials`, `constraints_func`, `targets`, `msg`, `feasible_trials`, `infeasible_trials`, `has_constraints`, `trial`, `constraints`, `best_trials`, `non_best_trials`, `_targets`, `n_targets`, `metric_names`. No other names are tracked.

Definitions (defs): (a) every parameter of the function is defined at the line of the `def _get_pareto_front_info(` keyword, at the start of each invocation (all five parameters always count as bound there, whether passed explicitly or defaulted); (b) an assignment statement `name = ...` defines `name` at the line where that statement begins; (c) an augmented assignment `name op= expr` is BOTH a use of the reaching definition of `name` and a new definition of `name` on that line (the use happens first); (d) a `for name in iterable:` header redefines `name` at the header line each time a new iteration starts (the iterable expression on the header line counts as a use of the names it reads, on the header line, each time the header line executes).
Uses: a use of a tracked variable is any read of that name in the frame of `_get_pareto_front_info` (as a plain value, as the object of an attribute access or method call such as `name.attr` or `name.append(...)`, as a call argument, inside an f-string, in a condition, etc.). Within one statement all reads happen before that statement's own definitions (so in `x = f(x)` the read sees the previous definition). For an `if`/`elif` the use is on the line of the condition; for a `for` loop, on the header line. A statement that spans several physical lines (a call, a `raise`, a `return` with arguments on following lines, a parenthesized expression) is attributed entirely to the line on which the statement begins: all its uses and defs are reported on that first line. Names bound or read inside lambda bodies, inside the element/condition part of comprehensions or generator expressions, and anywhere inside the bodies of the nested functions `_make_trials_with_values` and `_infer_n_targets` are NOT part of this frame: their loop/parameter names are not tracked and reads there are not uses (the outermost iterable of a comprehension/generator expression IS evaluated in this frame, so reads in it are uses on the line where the enclosing statement begins). In particular, the parameter `targets` of the nested function `_make_trials_with_values` is a different variable from the tracked `targets`.
A def-use pair (variable, def_line, use_line) is observed when, during some invocation, the value bound by the definition of `variable` at def_line is the one read at use_line (i.e. no other definition of `variable` executed in between along the actual execution path of that invocation). Definitions never reach across invocations.

All line numbers are absolute, 1-based line numbers in `optuna/visualization/_pareto_front.py` as it exists in the repository.

Answer as a JSON object {"observed_def_use_pairs": [...]} whose list contains one object per unique observed pair, with exactly the keys `variable` (string, the bare variable name exactly as spelled in the source, e.g. `"foo_bar"`, including any leading underscore), `def_line` (JSON integer) and `use_line` (JSON integer). Each unique (variable, def_line, use_line) triple appears exactly once, no matter how many times or in how many invocations it was observed. Sort the list ascending by `variable` (plain string comparison of the names, i.e. Python's default `str` ordering, in which `_` sorts before lowercase letters), then by `def_line`, then by `use_line`.
